items.excerpt: Suno unveiled a new downloads policy, output watermarking/fingerprinting, clearer community guidelines and 'transparency tools' for identifying AI tracks. The changes restrict mass distribution of Suno songs to streaming platforms while preserving pro and personal use.
items.rationale: Suno's new download/watermarking rules directly change what producers can legally do with generated tracks starting now.

items.excerpt: Suno is the first customer of Musixmatch's Sentinel, which screens AI prompts and generated outputs for copyrighted compositions, lyrics and music. Prompt-level filtering becomes part of the generation pipeline itself.
items.rationale: Copyright screening moves into the prompt box itself — a new constraint every AI-music workflow will feel.

items.excerpt: Distributor Symphonic has partnered with ArtyShield to give clients free access to MusicShield, a tool designed to protect tracks from unauthorised AI use before they are released. Pre-release protection becomes a standard step in the delivery chain.
items.rationale: Pre-release anti-AI protection arrives free inside a major distributor — a concrete new step in the release checklist.

items.excerpt: An anonymous producer alleges in a new lawsuit that Kanye West's Vultures II and Bully used AI, and seeks compensation for uncredited work. The suit puts AI credit and disclosure inside a major-album production dispute.
items.rationale: AI credit and disclosure land inside a major-album lawsuit — the first real test of who gets paid on AI-assisted records.

items.excerpt: Sylvan Esso on making Ow in their self-built studio, why they pulled their music from Spotify, and why 'Suno isn't coming up with that anytime soon'. A craft counter-argument to prompt-based music making.
items.rationale: A working duo spells out what a self-built studio still does that prompting cannot — the craft counterweight of the week.
